blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
The last mile is the final step of delivery. It is the short journey from a local depot to the customer's door. It sounds short, but it is often the hardest and most expensive part of the whole chain.

Why is it so hard? Because it is many small trips, not one big one. Every address is different. Traffic gets in the way. The customer may not be home. A single parcel may need two or three attempts.

Companies that get the last mile right usually win their customers' loyalty. The ones that do not hear about it very quickly.

items.q: What is the last mile?
options: A long journey between two cities
The final step from a local depot to the customer's door
The trip from the port to the depot
The first step in the factory
items.why: "The last mile is the final step of delivery… from a local depot to the customer's door."

items.q: Why is the last mile expensive?
options: Because the depot is far from the port
Because the parcels are very heavy
Because it is one big trip
Because it is many small trips, not one big one
items.why: "it is many small trips instead of one big one."

items.q: What can make a single parcel need two or three attempts?
options: The customer may not be home
items.why: "The customer may not be home. A single parcel may need two or three attempts."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which idea?
options: The last mile is hard to plan.
The last mile is easy because it is short.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que "soa curto, mas é a parte mais difícil" — logo, o autor discorda de que seja fácil por ser curto.

items.q: "The ones that do not hear about it very quickly" suggests that…
options: customers complain fast when delivery is bad
companies never find out about mistakes
items.why: Inferência: "hear about it" = os clientes reclamam rápido quando a última milha falha.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie orientando a líder de atendimento. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi. Let's talk about the last-mile team. This week we have had three kinds of problem, and each one feels different to the customer. I want you to see the difference.

The first one is traffic. The van has left the depot on time, but the roads are slow, so the parcel arrives late. The customer is annoyed, but they still get the box the same day.

The second one is the address. The address on the label is wrong or hard to find. The driver has tried, but they cannot reach the door. This one is worse, because the customer waits at home for nothing.

The third one is the missed attempt. The customer is not home, so we try again tomorrow. We have made two attempts on some parcels this week. That is expensive for us and slow for them.

So, same team, three problems. Traffic is late but done. A bad address is a wasted trip. A missed attempt costs us twice. When you answer a call, listen for which one it is. That tells you what to say and how to help.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many kinds of problem does Sophie describe this week?
items.why: "this week we have had three kinds of problem."

items.q: What happens with the traffic problem?
options: The parcel is late but still arrives the same day
The van does not leave the depot
The customer never gets the box
items.why: "the parcel arrives late… they still get the box the same day."

items.q: Why is a wrong address worse than traffic?
options: Because the customer waits at home for nothing
items.why: "the customer waits at home for nothing."

items.q: Why does Sophie say a missed attempt "costs us twice"?
options: Because the team must try again another day
Because two vans are needed at once
Because the parcel is very expensive
items.why: Inferência: "we try again tomorrow… two attempts" — repetir a viagem custa de novo.

items.q: Why does Sophie want the lead to know which problem it is?
options: So she can fire the driver
So she knows what to say and how to help the customer
So she can raise the price
So she can close the depot
items.why: Inferência: "That tells you what to say and how to help" — o tipo de falha guia a resposta ao cliente.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The van picks up the parcels at the depot." A depot is…
options: a local base where goods are stored
items.why: Depot = depósito/base local de onde saem as entregas.

items.q: "Please check the address on the label." An address tells you…
items.why: Address = endereço, o lugar da entrega.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The driver made two ___ but no one was home."
items.why: Attempt = tentativa; duas tentativas de entrega.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Good service keeps customers happy and builds their ___."
items.why: Loyalty = lealdade; bom serviço faz o cliente ficar.

items.q: "The last mile is the most expensive part." Expensive means…
options: it costs a lot of money
items.why: Expensive = caro, custa muito.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem no trabalho de entrega. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We will roll out the new delivery app next month." To roll out means to…
options: start using it step by step
items.why: Roll out = colocar em uso, aos poucos.

items.q: "The manager has to sign off on the new routes." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "The driver said he would call, but he did not follow through." This means he…
options: did not finish what he promised
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "When a parcel is late, please follow up with the customer." To follow up means to…
items.why: Follow up = dar retorno/checar depois com o cliente.

items.q: "If we miss too many attempts, customers will push back." To push back means to…
items.why: Push back = resistir, reclamar.
